cases.title: Case B: Volatile Memory Forensics
cases.subtitle: Windows 10 RAM Capture & Process Injection Detection
cases.summary: Analyzed a 16 GB Windows RAM capture using Volatility 3 to uncover stealth process hollowing and unauthorized command & control channels.
bullets: Flagged svchost.exe (PID 4812) running illegally under parent cmd.exe (PID 3920).
Discovered active TCP socket connection to C2 IP 198.51.100.45:8443.
Detected injected MZ header in VAD memory section with PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE permissions.
cases.terminal_output:
$ python3 vol.py -f memdump.raw windows.pstree
Name                PID    PPID   Time Created
system              4      0      12:00:00
 |- services.exe    640    492    12:00:05
 |   |- svchost.exe 892    640    12:00:08 (Legitimate)
 |- cmd.exe         3920   2140   14:15:22
     |- svchost.exe 4812   3920   [ANOMALOUS PARENT CMD]

$ python3 vol.py -f memdump.raw windows.netscan
TCPv4 192.168.1.105:49210 -> 198.51.100.45:8443 ESTABLISHED PID:4812

cases.title: Case C: Browser Artifact Reconstruction
cases.subtitle: SQLite Web History Parsing & NTFS $MFT Timeline
cases.summary: Parsed Chrome and Firefox SQLite history stores to reconstruct the user browsing session leading up to infection, cross-referencing against NTFS $MFT file creation timestamps.
bullets: Extracted Chrome urls and downloads SQLite databases.
Matched search query 'invoice update download free' at 14:10:05 UTC.
Correlated download completion time with NTFS creation timestamp of invoice_update.exe.
